title: Synthetic probe cadence and trace budget plan (Q4 instrumentation sprint)
content:
Context and goal:
This is the Q4 (timeboxed) plan to standardize synthetic probe cadence and impose a trace budget for inference pipelines. Goal: reduce investigation latency for regressions while keeping trace and query costs under our monthly threshold. Outcome expected by end of sprint: (1) compact probe naming and cadence scheme implemented across hosted/dedicated/private routes, (2) trace-budget enforcement and sampling policies in the router + collector, (3) a 6-panel compact dashboard template and runbook for oncall.

Why this is different
- Focus on cadence (when probes run) not just probe content. We want probes that exercise cold-cache, prefix-lookup, and fallback paths at orthogonal time slices so root cause isolation is easier.
- Explicit trace budget per tenant/route to avoid runaway costs during heavy sampling.
- Lightweight investigation-first dashboard wireframe optimized for SRE/operator triage flow.

High-level timeline (2-week sprint chunks)
- Week 1: finalize cadence taxonomy, pick canonical probe payloads, add probe tags for model/route/tenant.
- Week 2: implement collector-side sampling limiter and per-tenant quotas. Instrument router to emit trace-budget-metrics.
- Week 3: integrate sampling policy with rollout feature flags, bake canary probes. Create compact dashboard skeleton and alerts.
- Week 4: run guided oncall tabletop, iterate on thresholds, document runbook and ship.

Probe cadence taxonomy (recommended defaults)
- Hot-path micro-probe: every 1m (lightweight prompt ~50 tokens) to surface tail-latency and token generation regressions. Low payload cost, low trace sampling.
- Warm-path probe: every 5m (longer prompt ~200 tokens) exercising KV-cache, batching behavior. Sample 1/500 traces by default.
- Cold-start probe: every 15m per region (simulates cold model container, full initialization). Heavy weight; sample 100% traces for first 30s after container spawn, then 1/10 afterwards.
- Canary rollout probe: triggered on canary deploy events and immediately for 30 minutes after rollout; high sampling (1/5) and additional quality checks (top-k EM/QA metrics).
- Ad-hoc investigative probes: run-on-demand via console (devs/operators) with explicit high-sample flag.

Mandatory probe metadata fields (instrumentation contract)
- probe_id (string): prefix garden-probe|prod|route|model|scenario
- owner (string): team or person responsible
- cadence (string): e.g., 1m, 5m, 15m
- scenario_tags (list of short strings): e.g., [cold-start, fallback, kv-warmth]
- expected_sli (string): latency_p50<120ms or generation_quality>.9
- payload_signature (string): short hash or schema id
- trace_sampling_tier (string): low|medium|high

Key metric definitions (compact, operator-friendly)
- probe.latency_ms: end-to-end generation time measured at router entry to final token sent (ms). Unit: ms. Aggregation: p50/p90/p99 over 5m windows.
- probe.prefix_kv_hit_rate: fraction of requests that hit prefix/KV cache. Unit: ratio. Aggregation: avg over 30m.
- probe.cold_init_time_ms: cold container init time (ms) measured for cold-start probes. Aggregation: raw and p95.
- probe.quality_score: automated quality check for canary probes (0-1). Calculation: weighted discrete checks (toxicity, hallucination heuristics, n-gram overlap).
- probe.trace_budget_consumed: counter of traces emitted against budget threshold. Unit: traces. Aggregation: sum per tenant per hour.

Trace sampling & budget enforcement
- Design: enforce a hard per-tenant/month trace cap (configurable). When cap reached, reduce sampling to minimal emergency tier (only errors and highest-severity probes).
- Priority order for sampling when constrained: Canaries (retain), Cold-start (retain for 30s post-spawn), Hot-path low-sample (downscale), Warm-path (downscale), Ad-hoc (respect opt-in quota).
- Admission control in collector: collector maintains sliding-window counter for tenant traces and signals router to throttle trace emission at source via header flag (X-Trace-Sampling).
- Budget telemetry: metric: trace_budget.remaining_ratio per tenant, and per-route sampled_ratio. Alert when remaining_ratio < 0.15.

Sampling policy examples (defaults)
- Small tenant (<100k req/mo): hot 1/1000, warm 1/500, cold 1/10 for 5min after init, canary 1/2.
- Enterprise tenant (reserved capacity): hot 1/200, warm 1/100, cold 1/5 for 2min after init, canary 1/1.
- Shared prod routes (public): hot 1/2000, warm 1/1000, cold 1/20, canary 1/5.

Dashboard wireframe (6-panel compact layout)
1) Global health strip: p50/p90/p99 probe.latency_ms (sparkline), trace_budget.remaining_ratio (bar). Quick status icons per region.
2) Route selector + top-3 probes: drop-down to change route/model. Shows latest probe pass/fail and quality_score.
3) Cold-start panel: cold_init_time_ms heatmap by region + recent container spawn events.
4) KV-warmth and prefix hit panel: probe.prefix_kv_hit_rate histogram + cold/warm split.
5) Sampling and trace budget panel: traces emitted vs budget per tenant (hourly), alert markers when low.
6) Investigation timeline: clickable probe run list with trace links, raw prompt snippet (redacted), quick-copy to replay button.

Runbook: first 6 actions for an oncall detecting latency regression
1) Check Global health strip and identify affected region/route.
2) Open investigation timeline and find latest failing probe id. Copy probe payload and run locally if required.
3) Inspect cold-start panel: if cold_init spikes align with regressions, check deployment/instance churn.
4) Examine KV-warmth: low prefix_kv_hit_rate => possible cache eviction or routing change.
5) If trace budget low, toggle high-sample override for this tenant temporarily (console button) and capture traces.
6) Escalate to platform infra if container init or kernel error patterns show in traces.

Alerting guidance
- Latency regression alert: if route p95 latency increases >30% of baseline for 10m AND probe.quality_score drops for canary, fire P1.
- Trace budget warning: remaining_ratio < 0.15 -> warn to owners. remaining_ratio < 0.05 -> auto-throttle sampling and page owners.
- Cold-start storm: >5 cold-starts per region in 10m -> page infra.

Operational knobs for cost control (implementation notes)
- Hierarchical sampling config: global default -> org -> tenant -> route -> probe-level. Override order must be deterministic.
- Backoff policy: when budget high-churn detected, decrease warm/hot sampling rates by configurable factor (x0.1) for up to 2 hours.
- Query-cost tagging: every probe invocation must attach cost_estimate_usd label (best-effort) so dashboards can project spend per probe pattern.

Rollout instrumentation checklist
- Add probe metadata and tags for new route (owner, cadence, expected_sli).
- Add sampling tier and initial budget estimate for tenant.
- Ensure router emits X-Trace-Sampling hints and trace_budget.metric.
- Add route to compact dashboard config (small YAML row).
- Run canary probes and validate quality_score thresholds before promoting.

Open questions / decisions required
- Centralized vs distributed trace counters: do we rely on collector atomic counters or allow eventual consistency with best-effort throttling? Decision needed—leaning toward collector central counter for accuracy at cost of complexity.
- Budget reset semantics for trial tenants: monthly vs rolling-30d. Ops preference?
- Level of payload redaction required in probe payloads saved in timeline (PII/PHI concerns).

Next steps (owner action items)
- Sofia: land probe metadata schema change in telemetry repo (PR #98 suggested).
- Ethan: prototype collector-side quota counter, spike test with synthetic tenants (Jira OBS-412).
- Priya: sketch dashboard and alert panels, run tabletop with SREs week of Oct 7.

Notes to reviewers (quick)
- This is intentionally operator-first: compact and actionable, not an exhaustive metric catalog. We will follow with a metric census doc if we land these defaults.
- Please call out any regulatory constraints about storing prompts in the timeline; we should default to hashed prompt signatures unless the route is explicitly allowed.

Appendix: short example probe_id strings
- garden-probe|prod|route-chat-compress|gpt-medium|hot-1m
- garden-probe|stage|route-embed|basemodel-x|cold-15m

End of doc.
